summary:
Scope: the live behaviour of cycles #37-#46 (2026-09-29 14:47 to 2026-09-30 15:04 UTC, $6.06 in all), from R1 = 281e8edf…141055.txt (0.12.0, 12:10 UTC) and R2 = fdd5866d…171054.txt (0.13.0, 15:10 UTC). Line numbers below are R2's unless marked.

Verdict: the agent now follows the code-kept structures when they force it. It answers owner messages first when code makes the cycle ordinary (#42, #46). It filed its first upgrade request (Printify), which was released 3 hours later. It caught a critical formula bug before listing (#39/#41). It respects the focus burn mode and has made no NEVER-class move. Its business judgement is still supply-driven and unreliable:
- **No work on demand or traffic.** No plan step worked on search visibility or traffic for the 6 live listings, which have 4 views in all. knowledge_search was called 0 times, and the owner's 44 library learnings are contradicted by the live listings. Research was $0.40 of 09-30's $4.66 (8.7%), all on POD costs.
- **Where the money went.** 57% of 09-30's spend went to 3 workshop runs. The $1.84 one produced 3 sheet pictures that were never used.
- **Photo QA is still behind.** It is the first obligation in every plan and the owner flagged it 5 times. #42 listed a product with 2 photos against the agent's own lesson written 16 hours earlier. #46 deferred the photos "for tomorrow's budget", although make_image is free, and spent $0.35 on a Pillow poster.
- **The POD plan's numbers drifted.**
  - The landed cost went €14.95 (Printify, #43), then €10.98 (Gelato, #45), then "roughly €8 margin" at Printify (#46).
  - The base cost can't be known before an owner approval, and sizes are mislabelled.
  - There is no project or demand note, so the proposal would be refused.
  - Its decision dates (10-15, 10-21, 10-29, 11-29) fall after the projected runway end, about 10-18 at the current $4.89/day.
- **Honesty slips.**
  - It told the owner "HTML/CSS" but drew with Pillow.
  - A demand note cites a generic Etsy SEO article (library #1) as demand evidence.
  - It called a code-graded "marketing" page "independent".
  - It claimed fixes and verifications that did not happen.
  - Product text says a human designed and checked it.
- **Memory is stale.**
  - STRATEGY is unchanged since #35 and still puts dropshipping first.
  - No lesson has been written since #40, and 0 memory writes happened on 09-30. The photo lesson still says 3+ while the code's minimum is 5.
  - Dropshipping #3 is stuck at "proposed" with no numeric case or critique; the knock-outs never saw it.
- **Truncation hides the new steering.** TODAY'S REVIEW loses its focus and lesson (1,262 bytes cut), and ROADMAP hides the POD first-test milestone #8 (737 bytes cut). The two costliest cycles (#44, #46) lost their handoffs to worst-case stops.
- **The owner is still QA, art director and provider chooser.** The owner:
  - flagged the photos 3 times (#52, #55, #58);
  - called the new photos duplicates twice (comments on approvals #12 and #13);
  - reversed Gelato and set the design brief (#62);
  - reset the cost estimates;
  - raised the daily cap from $5 to $7.

observations.topic: Photo obligation and owner QA deferred; the photo mistake repeated
observations.finding:
'Live listings with fewer than 5 photos' has headed OBLIGATIONS in every plan since 0.12.0 (R1:381, R2:422). At 17:10 it still lists 4 listings (3, 3, 3 and 2 photos).
- #42 knowingly proposed the Nebenkosten listing with 2 photos ('2 is minimum-viable to launch — I'll add a 3rd next cycle'). That was 16 h after the agent wrote lesson c40, 'Every Etsy listing needs 3+ photos before proposing it', and after the owner had flagged photos three times (#52, #55, #58).
- #43 and #45 were venture cycles, which have no make_image, so the photos were correctly deferred there.
- #46 was an ordinary cycle. Its plan said 'Photo fixes on the 4 short listings need make_image calls and will wait for tomorrow's budget', then spent $0.35 on a poster workshop. make_image is not a paid call, and a work step costs about $0.018 (#42: 14 steps for $0.248). The three sheet renders bought in #44 were sitting in workshop/out.
- The 'duplicates' the owner flagged were structural: #40 made photos 2 and 3, and #42 photos 4 and 5, each from the same page (e.g. en_resume_template.pdf#1 for both photo4 and photo5).
- #42 looked at only one of each pair before proposing.
observations.evidence: #42: reply #389 at R2:854; propose_etsy_listing #485 at R2:883 (2 photos); approval #14 description at R2:1399 ('Only 2 photos now'). Lesson c40 at R2:545. Owner messages #52/#55/#58 at R2:1425, 1422, 1419. Approval comments #12/#13 ('additional pictures just seem like duplicates') at R2:1400-1401. #40 make_image rows R2:1024-1027. #42 make_image rows 866-869 (both resume photos from en_resume_template.pdf#1). #46 plan assessment at R2:582.
observations.likely_cause_in_code: A QA defect never makes a cycle ordinary; only messages, due promises, decisions and misses do (agent/obligations.py:140-159; agent/loop.py:358-373). Venture cycles lack make_image (agent/tools.py:140-160). The agent's lesson says 3+ while qa.MIN_PHOTOS = 5 (integrations/qa.py:21).

observations.topic: How $1.84 went on one workshop run (#44)
observations.finding:
How the run came about:
1. The Opus plan asked for 3 make_image photos of spreadsheet sheets ('Umlageschlüssel sheet close-up…') that existed only inside the .xlsx.
2. The worker made one turn with 3 parallel make_image calls using pages 'shop/nebenkostenabrechnung_de.xlsx#1', and all were refused. That is one mistake ×3 in a single turn, not three attempts. Neither report shows it earlier.
3. After workspace_list showed a single preview PNG, it launched a workshop to render all 3 sheets ('I need 2 more distinct workshop-generated images since only one preview exists'). The reply gives no cost reasoning. It did not reuse the #41 script that already rendered a sheet (workshop/scripts/open-shop-nebenkostenabrechnung-de-2.py).

The cost:
- Quoted $0.348, charged $1.838 (5.3×: 540,865 cache-write and 2,008,335 cache-read tokens). That is above the owner's workshop_run_cap_usd of $1.50.
- The overrun stopped the cycle, so there was no look, no edit and no journal. The owner then reset the estimate factor (12:26).
- The workshop also 'computed formula values manually in Python' and rendered only tenants A and B, so the pictures may not match what the workbook computes.
- 5 hours later the PNGs are unused. On 09-30 the 3 workshop runs cost $2.64 of $4.66 (57%).
- No lesson was written ('make_image takes PDF/PNG pages', 'reuse scripts').
observations.evidence: Cycle #44: plan R2:684-702; refusals R2:719-721; reply #422 R2:714; workshop #522 R2:723. observations.likely_cause_in_code: The run cap is checked against the pre-call quote only (agent/workshop.py:205-210), so a single code-execution call can overrun it. The plan context doesn't show which pages exist for make_image. A worst-case stop skips the reflection.

observations.topic: The print-on-demand plan (posters at €20-35, €6.09 shipping, 3 posters by 10-07)
observations.finding:
What the data shows:
- **Margin drift.**
  - #43: Printify/Posterflow landed about €14.95, so €22 keeps €3.98 ('need €24-26').
  - #45: switched to Gelato (€5.29 + €5.69 = €10.98), so €22 keeps €7.92. The 50x70 figure of '€17' was a guess.
  - #46: back on Printify (OPT OnDemand #443, DE shipping €6.09/€6.29), but the plan's money path says '€20-35 … roughly €8 margin' with the Printify base cost unknown. That €8 comes from the Gelato numbers.
- **Base cost.** The integration only learns it after the owner approves a product (the catalog has none).
- **The bar was lowered.** #46 relies on the code's 15% gate ('propose_printify_product will reject if margin <15%'). That gate is weaker than the agent's own €5-per-poster bar: at an €8.25 base (the '$9.08' evidence) a €20 price passes the code with €2.80 net.
- **Sizes mislabelled.** It wrote 16.5x23.4" as '~A4 landscape' (it is A2) and 33.1x23.4" as '~50x70cm' (it is A1).
- **The proposal would be refused.** There is no POD project and no demand note, and propose_printify_product requires both (tools.py:3617-3624). #46's plan has neither step.
- **Dates disagree.** Promise #1 and message #63 say 10-07; the same plan's money path says live by 10-15; milestone #2 is 10-15; milestone #8 is 10-21; continue/stop is 10-29 and 11-29. Runway is 18.3 days (to about 10-18).
- **Duties not disclosed to the owner.** Pitch #56: '~30 min, no cash upfront'. Missing: GPSR responsible-person and safety information, VerpackG/LUCID packaging registration, the 14-day withdrawal right with return costs, and 19% USt if the owner isn't a Kleinunternehmer (−€3.51 at €22).
- **Demand evidence.** One 'independent' page (a single Etsy listing) and vendor pages.
- **Design.** The chosen design (a generic Bauhaus composition with 'SCHÖN') replaced #43's evidence-picked designs without a demand note.

Judgement: acceptable as a small probe (no stock, listing fee about €0.18). But on these numbers it would set prices near break-even and decide after the money runs out. It should:
- set the floor from the €5 bar (≥ about €25 at an €8 base);
- create the project and demand note first;
- judge the posters at day 14 (10-14), not 11-29.

Owner backing R2:1344. Milestones #2/#8 at R2:1356, 1363. Runway R2 ECONOMY 199-250. My check with app/agent/econ.fees and integrations/printify.keeps (scratchpad/behaviour): €22 with €6.09 shipping keeps €7.52 / €4.56 / €1.81 at a base of €5.29 / €8.25 / €11; least_price(€8.25) = €20.00.

observations.topic: Honesty and accuracy toward the owner and buyers
observations.finding:
- **(a) The poster method.** Message #63 told the owner 'Designing poster #1 now (Bauhaus-style, HTML/CSS …)'. One turn later the workshop task said 'since no internet/browser is available, instead draw the design directly with PIL'. No correction was sent; the cycle stopped. The owner's premise, that Ember has HTML/CSS design tools, was never corrected.
- **(b) A demand note with no demand evidence.** The first demand note (#42) was refused for its source 'library #1 (Etsy search factors) + general knowledge of §556 BGB'. The agent then cited just 'library #1', a generic Etsy-search article, and the gate passed. The note has no demand numbers, although #37's research had returned relevant pages (including an Etsy Nebenkosten listing and a free Excel template at vermieterwelt.de).
- **(c) A grade restated.** #45 saved Gelato's price page and the code graded it 'marketing … weigh it lightly'. The same cycle wrote 'independent structured data' into the venture and 'Gelato publishes real EU pricing (independent source)' to the owner.
- **(d) Claims of work that wasn't done.**
  - #42's message said 'Fixed this cycle — proposing edits … the other under-5-photo listings up to 5 photos each'. It was the cycle's first tool call; only 2 listings were proposed, and 4 are still short.
  - Project #7's note says 'Formulas verified via preview screenshot', but the preview shows only the first sheet (Stammdaten). The real check was #41's workshop.
- **(e) Product text claims human work.** Live products say 'designed and checked by a human' (EN tracker and budget specs), 'von einem Menschen gestaltet und geprüft' (DE specs) and 'Designed by the shop owner … reviewed by a human' (EN resume). #42 added 'alle Inhalte wurden von einem Menschen geprüft' to the Nebenkosten listing. Ember designed them, and the owner's review is a click: on 09-30 three approvals took 83 s (12:00:59-12:02:22).

(d) R2:1418 (#59), R2:1333 (project #7 notes), R2:1238/1241 ('Picture of the first sheet'). (e) R2:2306, 2372, 2438, 2490 (specs), R2:1021 (EN resume description), R2:716 (Nebenkosten description); approvals R2:1399-1401.
observations.likely_cause_in_code: demand.source_problem accepts any existing library document (agent/demand.py:29-44). The agent's wording isn't checked against who did the work; the code's own line, integrations/etsy.py:68 ('designed with the help of AI and reviewed by the seller'), is accurate.

observations.topic: Provider flip-flop against its own upgrade request
observations.finding:
Three positions on the provider in 3 h 6 min, each stated as a decision:
1. 11:57, #59: files upgrade #1 (Printify integration) and asks for the token.
2. 12:04, #60: Printify, with a €24-26 floor.
3. 12:40, #61: 'Chose Gelato over Printify', because Printify's feed hides base costs, and plans to ask the owner to connect Gelato. This came 43 minutes after its own Printify request, and the integration it requested is exactly what reveals the real costs.

At 13:21 the owner's #62 overrides it ('we'll settle on Printify … as the api integration is already being build'). Judgement: the #45 venture cycle ran on 0.12.0 and optimised one criterion (price transparency) while ignoring the owner's sunk setup and its own in-flight request.

observations.topic: 'Never answer my ideas with a no' vs FIX NOW 14 and the knock-outs
observations.finding:
FIX NOW 14 took the optimism rule out of the prompts. prompts.py:80-85 and 137-138 now say 'A no backed by data … is a result: park the venture'. But the owner's standing instruction #2 still says 'Never answer my ideas with a no', and the prompt ranks the owner's words first. The agent's memory hardened it:
- lesson 'No idea gets a no';
- strategy 'Every idea gets scored and added to tree, never rejected outright'.

What happened live:
- #49 (09-29 11:29) gave a data-backed no to dropshipping. The owner added the instruction at 13:08, and #35 reversed the no.
- Since then no venture has been parked by the agent. #3 sits in 'proposed' with the only negative verdict buried in its risks field ('only proceed if owner wants to fund the €50 test given thin realistic margins').
- #5-#7 (blog, recruiting, AI companion, all flagged 'park' in analysis §8) stay unscored ideas. Owner/seeded ideas are exempt from the 30-day triage park.
- Judgement: it also seems to suppress 'I can't'. The owner's HTML/CSS idea (#62) got 'yes, HTML/CSS' instead of 'no HTML renderer; Pillow instead, or an upgrade request'.

The knock-outs (cash > €20, vendor-only) would stop #3 today, but they run only on the way into 'proposed', which #3 reached on 0.11.x.

observations.topic: Dropshipping #3: 'proposed' with 0 research calls, left undecided
observations.finding:
The planner shows #3 as:
- '[proposed] … research: 0 calls · research budget: $0.60 of $0.60 left · business case: complete';
- 'your owner wants it researched next (2026-09-29)'.

The owner's research request (14:03) was already met by #38 (15:22), and #35/#38 made 5 dropshipping searches before research was bound to ventures (0.12.0). So '0 calls' and 'researched next' are artefacts.

What stands:
- There is no numeric case (venture_cases 0) and no critique.
- Its sources are vendor/affiliate pages (zikanalytics, BigBuy/CJ).
- Its first test needs €50 of ad money, above venture_cash_eur €20.
- In focus mode it isn't on READY.
- WAITING FOR YOUR OWNER says 'None', though the Ventures tab waits on the owner.

Nobody decides it. The agent could park it with the numbers but won't (see the 'no' rule).

observations.topic: Continuity: handoffs lost in the costliest cycles
observations.finding:
Of #37-#46, 4 journals were written by code, not the agent:
- #39 (the reflection was starved by 15 steps);
- #41 (the reflection hit max_tokens);
- #44 and #46 (worst-case stops).

That lost the handoff of the two dearest cycles ($2.00 and $0.52).

Effects:
- #42 misjudged #41: 'last cycle's plan apparently not executed'. In fact #41 fixed the xlsx and cover-letter photos, but it did skip the owner answer it had planned as step 1.
- #45 read #44 as 'failed on make_image page refs', although #44 had produced the renders.
- #46's digest lists 'Done (10) … and 2 more'. The two hidden items are obligation_done and the workshop that made bauhaus_poster_1.png, and WORKSPACE shows only the first 19 files. The next plan can't see that poster #1 exists; the knowledge file still says 'Next: design poster #1'. Risk of paying for it twice.
- When the agent did write a handoff, the next ordinary cycle used it (#42 next → #44 plan).

observations.finding:
- **Stale goal.** Milestone #3 'Nebenkosten tool live' has been met since 12:01 but is still an open goal 'due in 6 days' (#44 meant to close it, then stopped).

observations.topic: Spend vs burn mode, review target and cap
observations.finding:
The agent followed the focus burn mode to the letter: no brainstorms, venture cycles only on the backed #4 (#45: 'Burn mode is focus, so there are no brainstorms'). Spend did not follow it:
- 09-30 cost $4.66 by 17:10 local: workshop $2.64 (57%), work $1.07, research $0.40, plans $0.39, review/study/reflect $0.16.
- The review's focus was about $0.30/day; analysis §8 targeted about $1.90/day.
- The owner raised the daily cap from $5.00 (R1) to $7.00 (R2), against the analysis's $2.50, and reset the estimate factor after the $1.84 stop.
- 5 of the 12 cycles were woken by the owner, three of them within 12 minutes (#42 11:57, #43 12:01, #44 12:05).
- By leg on 09-30: Etsy digital $3.19 (68%, of which $2.30 in workshops for one listing's fix and photos), POD $1.47 (32%). Traffic: $0.

observations.topic: The owner is still QA, art director and strategist
Caught and fixed a critical product bug before listing
observations.finding:
Positive. #37 flagged the B18 reference, #39 found 'a critical formula bug', and #41 checked with a workshop run: 'the formulas reference wrong cells (off by 3 rows), which would make the tool completely broken for buyers'. #41 fixed it, sanity-checked tenant A's share with numbers, and copied the fix to shop/ before #42 listed the product.

My rebuild of the #37 spec with the app's own sheets.build confirms the bug was real. Mieterabrechnung divided by Stammdaten!B4 (the address text, since data starts at row 4 below a title) and multiplied by Kostenarten!B18 (an empty fill-in row). Every tenant row would have shown #VALUE!, and the chosen Umlageschlüssel per cost type was ignored. It would have shipped broken at €6.90.
observations.evidence: R2:1084 (reply #330), R2:941 (reply #367), R2:963-970 (workshop rows); project #7 note R2:1333; my rebuild: scratchpad/behaviour/nebenkosten_spec.json → neben.xlsx (Mieterabrechnung rows 4-11: '=B4/Stammdaten!B4', '=D4*Kostenarten!B18').

observations.topic: Owner channel and self-improvement loop now work
observations.finding:
